chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام:

About a man who comes to be in al-Baydāʾ, then an obligatory salat overtakes him, and he does not leave al-Baydāʾ until its time has passed: how should he deal with the salat, when praying in al-Baydāʾ has been prohibited?
So he said: “He should pray in it, and avoid the main path of the road.”

key_terms.الْبَيْدَاءِ: al-Baydāʾ, the desert location mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.فَرِيضَةٌ: an obligatory duty, meaning a required prayer
key_terms.قَارِعَةَ الطَّرِيقِ: the main beaten part of the road or roadway

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if the time of obligatory salat arrives while he is in al-Baydāʾ where prayer is discouraged?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about obligatory salat when a person is in al-Baydāʾ and cannot leave before the prayer time expires. Imam al-Hādī عليه السلام instructs that the person should perform the prayer there, while avoiding the middle or beaten part of the road.
